title: Document-as-Image Representations Fall Short for Scientific Retrieval
abstract: arXiv:2604.18508v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Many recent document embedding models are trained on document-as-image representations, embedding rendered pages as images rather than the underlying source. Meanwhile, existing benchmarks for scientific document retrieval, such as ArXivQA and ViDoRe, treat documents as images of pages, implicitly favoring such representations. In this work, we argue that this paradigm is not well-suited for text-rich multimodal scientific documents, where critical evidence is distributed across structured sources, including text, tables, and figures. To study this setting, we introduce ArXivDoc, a new benchmark constructed from the underlying LaTeX sources of scientific papers. Unlike PDF or image-based representations, LaTeX provides direct access to structured elements (e.g., sections, tables, figures, equations), enabling controlled query construction grounded in specific evidence types. translated_title: 图像化文档表示在科学文献检索中的不足
translated_abstract: 许多近期的文档嵌入模型基于“文档即图像”的表示进行训练，即将渲染后的页面作为图像而非底层源文件进行嵌入。与此同时，现有的科学文档检索基准（如 ArXivQA 和 ViDoRe）将文档视为页面的图像，从而隐性地偏向了这类表示方法。在本工作中，我们认为这种范式并不适合文本丰富的多模态科学文档，因为在这类文档中，关键证据分布在包括文本、表格和图表在内的结构化源文件中。为了研究这一场景，我们提出了 ArXivDoc，一个基于科学论文底层 LaTeX 源文件构建的新基准。与 PDF 或基于图像的表示不同，LaTeX 提供了对结构化元素（如章节、表格、图表和公式）的直接访问，从而支持基于特定证据类型的受控查询构建。我们系统地比较了纯文本、基于图像的表示方法
tldr: 本文提出基于 LaTeX 源文件构建的新基准 ArXivDoc，论证“文档即图像”的表示方法不适合科学文献检索任务，因为关键证据分布于文本、表格和图表等结构化源中。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces ArXivDoc, a new benchmark built from underlying LaTeX sources, demonstrating that document-as-image representations fall short for scientific retrieval where critical evidence is distributed across structured text, tables, and figures.
